policy.name: Nano loan v4 - inside the caps

notes.title: The policy cannot see another app's loan
notes.detail: nothing in this policy reads 'other_app_outstanding', so a borrower already holding 75,000 from other apps can be lent to again. The single-app cap can be satisfied while the aggregate one is broken, and only this field can tell the difference.

notes.title: The APR needs a policy rate to be legal
notes.detail: these charges imply an APR of about 30% over 1 months. The ceiling is 10x the policy rate, so this is inside it only while the policy rate is at least 3.0%. This lint does not hold a policy rate on purpose - it would go stale. Computed at the 30-day cap, because the policy states no term.

notes.title: A charge is priced per unit of time
notes.detail: 'late_fee 1% of limit per day' grows with how long the money is outstanding, which prices time rather than a service. For a Shariah-compliant product this has to become a one-off service charge, or a fee tied to a real cost that does not accrue.

notes.detail: the limit is capped at 50,000 and a single digital nano loan may not exceed 25,000 (SECP Circular 10 of 2023)

region.reading: The gap falls from 35.3% to 15.0% once income is held roughly still, so most of it is income reaching the decision through the policy's income rules rather than region itself. That is a product question - whether this product should serve lower incomes at all - not a defect in the rules.
region.not_a_verdict: This is a measurement, not a compliance opinion. Whether a variable is a legitimate business necessity is a legal question about the product, and nothing here can answer it.

employment.reading: The gap falls from 45.2% to 12.0% once income is held roughly still, so most of it is income reaching the decision through the policy's income rules rather than employment itself. That is a product question - whether this product should serve lower incomes at all - not a defect in the rules.
employment.not_a_verdict: This is a measurement, not a compliance opinion. Whether a variable is a legitimate business necessity is a legal question about the product, and nothing here can answer it.

discrimination.reading: Weak separation. A cutoff on this score will cut good and bad alike.
discrimination.caveat: Measured on the 24,622 borrowers who reached the scorecard. The 25,378 stopped by a gate are excluded, which flatters the figure whenever the gates are removing bad borrowers.

cutoff_sweep.what_the_best_threshold_means: The sweep lends at the best threshold (55), so the comparison with the policy's own cutoff is meaningful.
cutoff_sweep.in_sample_warning: The net-maximising threshold of 55 is chosen on the same 24,622 borrowers it is scored against. It is the best cutoff for this cohort's past, and an optimistic estimate for anyone it has not seen. Treat the shape of the curve as the finding, not the argmax.
